text.p: Portuguese cash bonds and futures were slightly lower as investors took profits across Europe but dealers said losses would be limited.
"There is a technical correction going on in futures and 10-year bonds but the selling isn't heavy," said one trader.
"If foreign bonds fall further we'll not lose as much as the Bund and the 10-year spread will narrow," he said.
Market opinion is divided over whether Portuguese inflation for June, due on Monday, will prompt the Bank of Portugal to cut rates.
"The yield curve could invert but not much. The disparity of forecasts for inflation, between 2.0 and 2.4 percent, will limit this," said another dealer.
"Most people will wait for the inflation number. If it is at the low end then shorter maturities will hit the roof," he said.
The escudo slipped against the mark in line with the French franc. At 1000 GMT it stood at 100.98/101.00 per mark against its closing 100.91/94.
